title: Mud Kitchen Deep-Dive
strapline: Real pots, real mud, real weather — a proper working kitchen outdoors where the messiest maths and richest talk happen.
intent: Children explore capacity, transformation and cause-and-effect through the endlessly satisfying business of mixing mud, water and nature.
Children build rich, sustained talk — recipes, orders, offers, negotiations — in a role-play that never runs dry.
Children develop hand and arm strength and coordination pouring, stirring, scooping and whisking with real utensils.
Children experience deep, immersive, self-directed play that they own completely — the adult is a guest here.
Children connect with the outdoors and the seasons, and learn that getting gloriously muddy is allowed and good.
implementation: Resource it for real: proper metal pans, wooden spoons, sieves, jugs, a working water source, a mud supply and a herb or flower patch to harvest.
Go beyond a single station — add a 'pantry' of loose parts (pine cones, petals, seeds, gravel), scales, and menus and chalkboards for recipes.
Stand back and let it run: resist tidying, directing or 'improving' the play — narrate and wonder aloud only when invited in.
Feed maths and language through play, not instruction: 'that's a full jug', 'how much water does your soup need?', 'whose is heaviest?'.
Keep it going all year — mud soup in the rain, frozen 'ice-cream' in winter, petal 'cakes' in summer — the kitchen reflects the season.
Sort the practicals so play stays free: waterproofs and wellies to hand, a hand-washing routine, and a tolerance for genuine mess.
key_questions: What are you cooking today — what's in it?
How much water does your mixture need?
Which pot is the heaviest now it's full?
What happened to the mud when you added more water?
Can you make a recipe for me to follow?

impact.text: Children explore capacity and comparison — full, empty, heavier, more — through pouring and mixing.
Children explore change and transformation as materials mix, thicken and freeze.
Children sustain rich role play with shared storylines, roles and negotiated props.
Children use talk within play to narrate, direct, offer and negotiate.
Children pour, scoop, stir and use tools with growing control and strength.

enhancements: A 'restaurant' extension with menus, a serving hatch, order pads and pretend money.
A herb and edible-flower patch beside the kitchen to harvest fresh ingredients.
Real kitchen scales and measuring jugs for weighing and measuring the 'ingredients'.
A seasonal special — frozen berry 'ice cream' in winter, blossom 'cupcakes' in spring.
A mud-recipe book of children's own dictated and illustrated concoctions.

playing_exploring: Children throw themselves into open-ended sensory play, exploring how mud and water behave.
The kitchen invites children to lead their own recipes, roles and stories.
active_learning: Deeply absorbing play keeps children engaged and returning day after day.
Children set their own goals — the perfect soup, a full pot — and persist to achieve them.
creating_thinking: Children plan recipes, predict what mixing will do, and adapt when it doesn't work.
They invent stories, menus and rules, thinking creatively within their play.
